properties.description:
County of Maui:
Received update for Maui County from Pacific Disaster Center, August 2013. 

Layer Name:Tsunami Evacuation Zones

File Name:tsun_evac_zones

Layer Type:Polygon

Status:Complete

Geog. Extent:Islands of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, Lanai, Maui and Hawaii

Projection:Universal Trans Mercator, Zone 4 (Meters)Datum:NAD 83 HARN

Description:Tsunami Evacuation Zones for the islands of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, Lanai, Maui and Hawaii Source:Island of Hawaii: Pacific Disaster Center (PDC), 1998.
Island of Oahu: City and County of Honolulu, 2010.Islands of Molokai, Lanai, Maui: County of Maui, 2013.Island of Kauai: County of Kauai, 2014
(Text written by PDC Staff, 1998):
Tsunami evacuation layers for the [islands of Hawaii and Kauai] were digitized from Tsunami
Evacuation Zone proof maps provided by  the State of Hawaii Civil Defense, andpublished in CountyTelephone Directories by GTE in 1991. 
These maps were produced by the Joint Institute for Marine and Atmospheric Research, at the University of Hawaii, in cooperation with the State of Hawaii Civil Defense System.
Data from these maps were digitized in the GIS program Arc View Version 3.0a using features from
island coastlines, roads, and the USGS 7.5 minute digital raster graphics (DRGs).  Specific distances given on the maps
(for example:  "1900 feet from Farrington Highway") were incorporated into the digitization.  Where no distances were
given, evacuation zone boundaries were estimated by topographical characteristics, or approximated using surrounding features such as roads.  In cases where evacuation zone boundaries bordered roadways, selected roads from state DLG road layer were extracted into
the tsunami evacuation shape file for accuracy.  No details of scale accompanied the paper proofs.  Coastline and evacuation
zone shape files for each island were then made into coverages using ArcInfo Version 7.1.2, which were subsequently appended
into a single coverage for editing.  Arcedit was used to eliminate all dangling nodes, intersections, etc. 
Tolerances were set to minimize the alteration of zone boundaries.  Topology was built for each island, polygons labeled, and polygon attribute tables created.  Each polygon is associated with a particular evacuation map, with the exception of two polygons on Oahu maps which are areas
of high ground (map #7), and water (maps # 18-19) within evacuation zones.A coverage for the State was created from appended individual island coverages in ArcInfo.

Other:
Merged all islands into one layer by OP Staff, August 2013, February 2014, October 2016.  
No information for fields MAPNUM and MAPNAME on Niihau, Kauai or Oahu.
Attributes:
Polygons:
ISLAND Island
Name
MAPNUM Map # of evacuation zone as it appears in the county telephone directory.
MAPNAME Geographic area covered by each numbered evacuation zone map, as it appears in the county telephone directory.
ZONE“1”= tsunami evacuation zone

Tsunami and Extreme Tsunami Evacuation Zone Maps – Cautions and Additional Information

For most Tsunami Warnings, evacuate out of the tsunami evacuation zones; in the
unlikely case of an “Extreme Tsunami” Warning, evacuate out of both the tsunami
evacuation zones and the extreme tsunami evacuation zones.

Remember:
  • Remain at least 100 feet away from inland waterways and marinas connected to the ocean due to wave surges and possible flooding
  • If possible, remove or deploy vessels to at least 50 fathoms (300 ft) deep and 2 miles away from harbor entrances; follow all directions from the Captain of the Port
  • Structural steel or reinforced concrete buildings of ten or more stories provide increased protection on or above the fourth floor
  • The evacuation zone is a guideline and should be considered the minimum safe evacuation distance
  • These maps do not consider the destructive effects of a locally generated tsunami. If you feel shaking, move inland immediately, well away from the evacuation zone
  • The evacuation zone is a guidance and should be considered the minimum safe evacuation distance

properties.snippet: All Hazard Alert Broadcast siren locations
properties.description:
This data compiled by the Washington Military Department on August 22, 2019. The All Hazards Alert Broadcasting System (AHAB) data points supply visual depiction of where the siren locations are along the Washington State Coast and some inland waterways. If an actual tsunami event occurs the sirens supply not only audible but visual warnings of the impending danger via a wailing audio sound and an intense blue light for the hearing impaired, which can also cut through fog and is visible from a long distance. The sirens further supply a 4500-watt public address system to relay verbal information to the local populations or play digitally pre-recorded messages. The siren design enables a 360-degree coverage. Has the capability to make test and actual evacuation announcements in English and Spanish (These are pre-recorded on each siren’s installed micro SD card.) Using pre-programmed phrases and words, messages can be created at any control point for such things as ‘Shelter in Place’, and Hazardous Material Notification. Siren positional data is derived from the satellite transponder attached to each siren which derives its location from current GPS satellites deployed by the United States.

Attribute Description

RTU - Siren reference number

Address - Nearest address of where the siren is located

Name - Name of the siren

LocationReference - Description of where the siren is located in relation to address

City - City where the siren is location

County - County where siren is located

Elevation - Elevation in feet AMSL of the siren location

Latitude - Latitude of siren location

Longitude - Longitude of siren location
Updated: 8/22/2019

TMK Parcels for affordable housing project.

Received from Jim Hayden, 5/24/17.
properties.description:
• Added GIS_Acres field
  • joined owndat.dbf downloaded 5/31/17
  • added link to Honolulu Real Property site

Steps used to create the Tier system:

  1. Ran Onyx ETL script to join own.dat table to parcel layer
  2. Turn on TMK, NormOwner, MajorOwner, BigstOwner, GISAcres.
  3. Unioned with the following layers:
    • TMK parcels, owndat.dbf (downloaded from County, 3/6/17)
    • SLUD (LUC, Feb 2016)
    • County Zoning (downloaded from County, 3/6/17)
    • 1/2 mile buffer from rail station (County, 2015)
    • 1/2 mile to 1 mile buffer from rail station (County, 2015)
    • 1/2 mile buffer from rail route (County, 2015)
    • 1/2 mile to 1 mile buffer from rail route (County, 2015)
    • 1/2 mile buffer from bus stops (County, 2012)
    • 1/2 mile to 1 mile buffer from bus stops (County, 2012)
    • 100 yr flood zone (County, 2014)
    • Tsunami Zone (County, 2010)
    • 1/2 mile buffer from sewer main (County, 11/21/2016)
    • 1/2 mile to 1 mile buffer from sewer main (County, 11/21/2016)
    • 1/2 mile buffer from water main (County, 2004)
    • 1/2 mile to 1 mile buffer from water main (County, 2004)
    • Reserves (DLNR, Jan 2017)
    • SMA (County, 2011)

  4. Queried from oahu_state_county_parcels_pltis_20170425_split:

    GISAcres_por >= 0.23 AND smarea = 0 AND ludcode <> 'C' AND (ZONE_CLASS = 'A-1' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'A-2' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'A-3' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'AG-1' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'AG-2' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'Aloha' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'AMX-1' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'AMX-2' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'Apart' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'ApartMix' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'BMX-3' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'BMX-4' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'C' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'IMX-1' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'Kak' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'MU' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'PU' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'Pub' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'R-10' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'R-20' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'R-3.5' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'R-5' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'R-7.5' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'ResMix' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'Resort' OR ZONE_CLASS = 'WI') AND NormOwner <> 'COUNTY BOARD OF WATER SUPPLY'

  • polygons >= 0.23 acres (or 10,000 sq ft)
  • parcels owned by State or County
  • State Land Use District Urban or Agricultural (No Conservation)
  • No SMA
  • No parcels owned by the Board of Water Supply
  • Includes the following County Zoning:
    • AG-1
    • AG-2
    • A-1
    • A-2
    • A-3
    • Aloha
    • Apart
    • ApartMix
    • Resort
    • R-3.5
    • R-5
    • R-7.5
    • R-10
    • R-20
    • AMX-1
    • AMX-2
    • WI
    • ResMix
    • BMX-3
    • BMX-4
    • IMX-1
    • C
    • MU
    • PU
    • Pub
    • Kak

Attribute Info;

  • TMK: 9 digit TMK Number (Numeric)
  • NormOwner: Owner name as described in owndat.dbf
  • MajorOwner: Owner name with Dept.
  • BigstOwner: State, State DHHL or County
  • GISAcres: Acreage of Full Parcel
  • TMK_txt: 9 digit TMK Number (String)
  • Fee_Owner: PLTIS Fee Owner (DLNR, 3/16/17)
  • Trust_Land_Status_s_: PLTIS Trust Land Status (DLNR, 3/16/17)
  • zone_class: County Zoning
  • rail_station_halfmile: within half mile of rail station (Yes/No)
  • rail_route_halfmile: within half mile of rail route (Yes/No)
  • bus_stop_halfmile: within half mile of bus stop (Yes/No)
  • fld_zone: 100 year flood zone
  • sewer_halfmile: within half mile of sewer main (Yes/No)
  • water_halfmile: within half mile of water main (Yes/No)
  • type: Reserve Type (Forest Reserve, State Parks, etc.)
  • smarea: SMA (0=No, 0=Yes)
  • ludcode: State Land Use Districts
  • GISAcres_por: Acreage of polygon (portion of full parcel)
  • zone: Tsunami Evacuation Zone (0=No, 1=Yes)
  • Tier: Tier Number
  • rail_route_half_to_1mile: within 1/2 to 1 mile of rail route
  • bus_stop_half_to_1mile: within 1/2 to 1 mile of bus stop
  • sewer_main_half_to1mile: within 1/2 to 1 mile of sewer main
  • water_main_half_to_1mile: within 1/2 to 1 mile of water main
  • rail_station_half_to_1mile: within 1/2 to 1 mile of rail station
  • Pt_Rail: Points for proximity to Rail Route
  • Pt_Sewer: Points for proximity to Sewer Main
  • Pt_Water: Points for proximity to Water Main
  • Pt_Owner: Points for Owner type
  • Pt_SLUD: Points for State Land Use District
    • 2 points: within 1/2 mile of rail route
    • 1 point: within 1/2 mile of sewer main
    • 1 point: within 1/2 mile of water main
    • 1 point: within 1/2 mile to 1 mile of rail route
    • 0.5 point: within 1/2 mile to 1 mile of sewer main
    • 0.5 point: within 1/2 mile to 1 mile of water main
    • 1 point: Non-DHHL State land or County land
    • 1 point: State Land Use Urban District
    • 0 point: DHHL State Land
    • 0 point: State Land Use Agricultural District
  • Pt_Bus: Not used
  • Score: Total Score of Pt_Rail + Pt_Sewer + Pt_Water + Pt_Owner + Pt_SLUD
  • Tier Scoring:
    • Tier 1: Score = 6 points and "No DHHL" and "Urban District Only"
    • Tier 2: Score = 4 to 5.5 points and "No DHHL" and "Urban District Only"
    • Tier 3: Score = All other parcels (Less than 4 points, DHHL lands, State Land Use Ag and Rural)
  • Revised, 6/5/17:
    • Added field "LandCover." This field is used to roughly determine the Land Cover of the parcel using latest Aerial data (ArcGIS World Imagery Basemap, WV2 imagery, and Google Earth).
      • 0 = Bare Land
      • 1 = <50% Structures
      • 2 = >50% Structures
    • Added field "Notes" to describe features about the parcel.
    • Created a new Tier 4 for road and drainage parcels that were removed from Tier 1.
